instruction.text: We can’t always see vibrations being made. Select the instruments whose vibrations we can’t see.

feedback.finish: Even though we can’t see the vibrations, they are still happening. When you blow into these instruments, the air inside them vibrates and creates a sound.

atoms.a: When Susie hits the tuning fork, it creates a ringing noise. What do you think happens to the fork when Susie hits it?
Susie now hits the fork and holds it into a bowl of water. What do you think will happen?

text: That’s right! The vibrations created by the tuning fork will transfer into the water, allowing us to see them.

instruction.text: Place your fingers gently on your neck and begin to hum. What can you feel?

feedback.end: When you speak, sing or hum, your vocal cords vibrate inside your neck. These vibrations, combined with the shapes you make with your mouth, create different sounds.

instruction.text: Decide what is vibrating in each example.

hint.text: The mouthpiece of an oboe has two pieces of reed, which the player blows on.
hint.label: Reed
